teams.product_capability: Learned legal distance metric that optimizes nearest-neighbor retrieval for jurist usefulness, exposed as a selectable map mode alongside the validated center_projected baseline and zero-shot citation/outcome hybrids
teams.question: Given v18 evidence that hierarchy_coherence is FUNDAMENTALLY UNPASSABLE at branch level (best purity 0.6497 < 0.70) and zero-shot cited_decisions_tfidf_outcome_hybrid_0.5 achieves JP=0.7990, LangDom=0.4911 (beating all supervised metric learning on full-harness production gates), does a Jurivoc-supervised metric learning approach fusing center_projected + cited_decisions_tfidf + outcome_tfidf + legal signals (sachverhalt TF-IDF, erwaegungen TF-IDF, norm/article embeddings, citation role weights) produce legally more useful nearest neighbors than the zero-shot hybrid baseline on jurist proxy benchmarks (branch_knn, legal_area_clustering, citation_heritage, tf_metadata_human_indexing) while maintaining zoom_coherence and multilingual_invariance?
teams.hypothesis: A metric learned from Jurivoc/TF weak labels CAN optimally weight complementary legal signals (facts for legal_area coherence, reasoning for citation proximity, norms for doctrinal proximity, citation roles for precedent proximity, cited decisions for citation heritage, outcomes for cross-lingual alignment) and suppress boilerplate, potentially beating the zero-shot cited_decisions_tfidf_outcome_hybrid_0.5 (JP=0.7990, LangDom=0.4911) on jurist proxy benchmarks. However, v18 evidence shows hierarchy_coherence is FUNDAMENTALLY UNPASSABLE — the embedding space captures legal reasoning proximity, not branch classification. This means Jurivoc/TF branch labels are the WRONG supervision target for legal proximity. The hypothesis is now: Jurivoc-supervised metric learning on LEGAL-AREA labels (normalized, 55 unique) rather than branch labels may yield gains, but the zero-shot hybrid baseline is extremely strong. This is a high-bar challenge requiring credible evidence of improvement beyond JP=0.7990, LangDom=0.4911.
teams.why_now: CONCRETE EVIDENCE UPDATE (v18 ACCEPTED): (1) hierarchy_coherence FUNDAMENTALLY UNPASSABLE at branch level (4 labels, best purity 0.6497 < 0.70) — Jurivoc/TF branch labels are WRONG supervision target for legal proximity. (2) Zero-shot cited_decisions_tfidf_outcome_hybrid_0.5 achieves JP=0.7990, LangDom=0.4911 — BEATS all supervised metric learning on full-harness production gates. (3) v17b REPRODUCED: legal_area label normalization (55 unique, cross-lingual) improves purity 15-25% across 4 seeds — correct supervision target is NORMALIZED LEGAL-AREA, not branch. (4) Core lane metric learning breakthrough: linear_metric_epoch4 JP=0.6847, mahalanobis_metric_epoch4 JP=0.6781 on center_projected space (frozen harness). (5) Cited_decisions_tfidf zero-shot achieves JP=0.6922, LangDom=0.6107 — beats supervised metric learning on jurist pairwise WITHOUT training. (6) All 6 cited_decisions_tfidf + center_projected hybrids PASS both adversarial gates. (7) Citation role modeling UNBLOCKED: 2,988 role annotations resolved; citing/following/criticizing PASS adversarial gates. (8) BOILERPLATE RESISTANCE CORRECTION: Real test shows 89-93% neighbor preservation when boilerplate removed — boilerplate NOT driving neighbors. (9) GPU unavailable; CPU-feasible variants only. SUPERSEDED because v18 fundamentally changes the supervision target (branch→legal-area) and zero-shot hybrid baseline now dominates.
teams.non_duplication: Core legal-distance lane performs UNSUPERVISED signal ablation (systematic combination/weighting of legal signals against frozen baseline) AND METRIC LEARNING on center_projected space (linear + Mahalanobis projections). This SUPERSEDED team pursued SUPERVISED METRIC LEARNING on weak labels (Jurivoc/TF metadata) fusing MULTIPLE legal signals including cited_decisions_tfidf AND outcome_tfidf. v18 evidence shows the original hypothesis (branch labels as supervision) is invalidated — legal-area normalization is the correct path. The SUPERSEDED charter documents this pivot; a future recharter would need new evidence that Jurivoc-supervised multi-signal fusion on NORMALIZED legal-area labels beats zero-shot hybrid (JP=0.7990, LangDom=0.4911).

teams.question: Given v18 evidence that hierarchy_coherence is FUNDAMENTALLY UNPASSABLE at branch level (embedding space captures legal reasoning proximity, not branch classification) and zero-shot cited_decisions_tfidf_outcome_hybrid_0.5 achieves LangDom=0.4911, JP=0.7990 with STRONG fractal hierarchy (HierAdv=+0.2918, ImpRate=90.3%), does CPU-feasible fine-tuning (LoRA/distillation) of multilingual-e5-small on Swiss Federal Supreme Court corpus with (a) HIERARCHY PRESERVATION LOSS on Leiden coarse/fine structure (NOT branch labels), (b) Jurivoc/TF NORMALIZED legal-area contrastive pairs, and/or (c) citation-heritage positive pairs produce embeddings that achieve adversarial_language_dominance < 0.49 AND jurist_pairwise_preference > 0.8 AND cross_language_retrieval > 0.2, while maintaining zoom_coherence improvement_rate >= 0.39 and NO hierarchy collapse on the frozen evaluation harness?
teams.hypothesis: multilingual-e5-small pretrained achieves BEST adversarial scores (LangDom=0.4877, JP=0.7017) but CATASTROPHICALLY COLLAPSES fractal hierarchy (1 coarse → 1000 fine clusters, hier_adv=0.0). v18 proves branch labels are WRONG for hierarchy preservation — the embedding space captures legal reasoning proximity, not doctrinal branch classification. A CPU-feasible LoRA fine-tuning with hierarchy preservation loss on LEIDEN CLUSTER STRUCTURE (validated fractal-map hierarchy, nesting=1.0, purity=0.9571) can retain superior cross-lingual alignment while restoring multi-resolution legal map structure. This is an independent path from metric learning (operates on native 384-dim multilingual space) and zero-shot hybrids (unsupervised). Supervised fine-tuning must beat zero-shot hybrid (JP=0.7990, LangDom=0.4911, HierAdv=+0.2918) on ALL gates to justify investment.
teams.why_now: CONCRETE ACCEPTED EVIDENCE UPDATE (v18): (1) hierarchy_coherence FUNDAMENTALLY UNPASSABLE at branch level — branch labels are WRONG target for hierarchy loss; must use Leiden cluster structure. (2) Zero-shot cited_decisions_tfidf_outcome_hybrid_0.5 achieves LangDom=0.4911, JP=0.7990, STRONG fractal — baseline to beat is HIGHER than before. (3) multilingual-e5-small pretrained: LangDom=0.4877, JP=0.7017, but hierarchy collapse — base architecture has superior cross-lingual signal. (4) GPU unavailable >2 director review cycles — CPU-feasible LoRA only. (5) Unsupervised cross-lingual alignment (proc_pairs, joint_pca) validated: proc_pairs LangDom=0.6799, Jurist=0.6981; joint_pca LangDom=0.6237, Jurist=0.6472. (6) Fractal-map validated: hierarchical Leiden nesting=1.0, purity=0.9571 — this is the CORRECT hierarchy preservation target. policy: Create specialized teams only for concrete product-relevant hypotheses or bottlenecks. Parallelism should grow with credible independent paths, not curiosity. Teams SUPERSEDED when evidence fundamentally invalidates hypothesis or baseline dominance makes further investment unjustified without new evidence.
